name: Conditional-Antimatroid Equivalence
hypotheses: Finite nonempty binary classes; coordinate reflections and constant coordinates are ignored in the graph formulation.
statement: Conditional antimatroids, bouquets of convex geometries, reflectively union-closed ample classes, and ample classes of Horn-renaming defect zero define the same one-inclusion graph class.
proof: The extremal-generation and local-extension formulations are the two standard finite definitions of conditional antimatroids. A reflected class has $H=0$ exactly when its complete minimal missing patterns have at most one positive bit, which is equivalent to union closure. An intersection-closed ample class contains its total intersection; after suppressing its fixed coordinates, partial-cube isometry supplies local one-element extension between comparable members, so it is a bouquet. Conversely every bouquet is ample and intersection closed.
